support_registry.text: 2. **Following a way creates stepwise liability rather than borrowed immunity.** Lexical evidence: `ٱتَّبِعُوا`, root `ت ب ع`, `B003` (stepwise tracking); `سَبِيلَنَا`, root `س ب ل`, `B001` (extended traversed way); and `شَىْء`, root `ش ي ء`, `B001` (a knowable thing). Structural cue: route-following precedes the guarantee, while the emphatic negation removes even one knowable portion of the followers' wrongs from the would-be carriers. Assigned role: path and tracking make participation cumulative; the negated “thing” closes the smallest imagined transfer. Abductive move: I infer that walking the offered route generates the follower's own responsibility even when another verbally claims it. Reading change: allegiance is a traversed practice with accruing consequences, not a slogan whose cost can be outsourced.

1. **The invitation is framed as a false indemnity contract.** Lexical evidence: `وَلْنَحْمِلْ / بِحَامِلِينَ`, root `ح م ل`, `B004` (guarantee and indemnity); `خَطَايَاكُمْ / خَطَايَاهُم`, root `خ ط ء`, `B002` (culpable wrongdoing); and `لَكَاذِبُونَ`, root `ك ذ ب`, `B004` (fulfilling or failing a charge). Structural cue: offer, categorical negation, and verdict occur in that order; `29:13` then assigns them their own loads plus additional ones. Assigned role: `حمل B004` gives the speech a legal-social shape, and `كذب B004` identifies failure of the assumed charge. Abductive move: the packet explicitly denies performance; I infer that the promise seeks to lower the follower's perceived cost by pretending liability is transferable. Reading change: the speech is not vague deception but an invalid surety offered to recruit followers.
